basis.governing_question: Which new point-of-sale system should Farmácias Lusas choose, and how can it be rolled out to run in all 40 pharmacies?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish what each pharmacy process area requires from a new point-of-sale system and where current practice falls short.

gate.label: Requirements sign-off
gate.decision: Go or no-go on starting vendor selection against the signed-off requirements?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Score vendors against the signed-off requirements and build the business case for the selection decision.

gate.label: Vendor selection
gate.decision: Which vendor's point-of-sale system is taken forward into implementation?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Configure the chosen system, prove it at one pilot pharmacy, and roll it out in waves to all 40.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the system as running in all 40 pharmacies and close the engagement?

workstreams.name: Process area requirements
workstreams.answers: What does each pharmacy process area require from a new point-of-sale system?
activities: Interview pharmacy staff on four process areas, two at once
Review operational data and documents on current practice
Consolidate requirements for sign-off at the gate

workstreams.name: Current practice gaps
workstreams.answers: Where does current practice in each process area fall short of what a new point-of-sale system requires?
activities: Compare current practice with the requirements by area
Observe daily work in pharmacies and note workarounds
Review findings with CEO, Operations Director, IT Manager

workstreams.name: Vendor shortlist and scoring
workstreams.answers: Which point-of-sale systems meet the signed-off requirements, and how do they score against them?
activities: Shortlist vendors against the signed-off requirements
Run vendor demonstrations with pharmacy staff and IT
Score each vendor against the signed-off requirements

workstreams.name: Business case for selection
workstreams.answers: Does any shortlisted point-of-sale system hold up in a business case for the selection decision?
activities: Estimate costs and benefits of each shortlisted system
Test cost assumptions against operational data
Prepare the evidence for the selection decision

workstreams.name: System setup and data load
workstreams.answers: Can the chosen system be configured for each process area and loaded with the pharmacies' data?
activities: Configure and test four process areas, two at a time
Rehearse loading pharmacy data into the configured system
Document readiness results for the workshop review

workstreams.name: Pilot pharmacy go-live
workstreams.answers: Does the configured system run stably in daily use at one pilot pharmacy?
activities: Go live at one pilot pharmacy after the readiness workshop
Track incidents and stability through daily use
Collect feedback from pilot pharmacy staff and customers

workstreams.name: Rollout, waves 1 and 2
workstreams.answers: How does the system go live in the first two waves of up to 10 pharmacies each?
activities: Train pharmacy teams before each wave goes live
Go live in two waves of up to 10 pharmacies each
Track stability and resolve issues after each go-live

workstreams.name: Rollout, waves 3 and 4
workstreams.answers: How does the system go live in the last two waves until all 40 pharmacies run it?
activities: Train pharmacy teams before each wave goes live
Go live in two waves of up to 10 pharmacies each
Confirm the system runs in all 40 pharmacies

deliverables.name: Interim requirements for first process areas
Requirements and gap findings for sign-off
Business case for the vendor selection decision
First configured process areas with test record
Readiness report with data load rehearsal results
Pilot pharmacy go-live record and stability report
Final readout with go-live record for all 40 pharmacies

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Secure access for the diagnostic work
events.decision: Is access to pharmacy staff and process data confirmed for the requirements work?
agenda: Present the diagnostic approach and the first six weeks
Discuss the pharmacy staff and process data the work needs
Confirm access to those people and data

events.label: Check-in: requirements
events.decision: Do the interim requirements stand as the basis for the remaining process areas?
agenda: Present the interim requirements for the first process areas
Discuss open questions for the remaining process areas
Confirm whether the interim requirements stand

events.label: Requirements sign-off
events.purpose: Sign off requirements and gap findings
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting vendor selection against the signed-off requirements?
agenda: Present the business requirements by process area
Review the requirements and gap findings for sign-off
Decide on starting vendor selection

events.label: Check-in: vendor scoring
events.decision: Do the shortlist and scoring hold as the basis for the selection gate?
agenda: Present the vendor shortlist against signed-off requirements
Review the vendor scoring against the requirements
Confirm the shortlist and scoring as the basis for the gate

events.label: Vendor selection
events.decision: Which vendor's point-of-sale system is taken forward into implementation?
agenda: Present the business case for the vendor selection decision
Review the vendor shortlist and scoring against requirements
Decide which vendor goes into implementation

events.label: Check-in: first build
events.purpose: Check the first configured process areas
events.decision: Does the test record support continuing with the remaining process areas?
agenda: Present the first configured process areas
Review the test record and any open issues
Confirm the approach for the remaining process areas

events.label: Workshop 1: pilot readiness
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting the pilot pharmacy go-live?
agenda: Present the readiness report with data load rehearsal results
Review the first configured process areas and their test record
Decide on go or no-go for the pilot pharmacy go-live

events.label: Check-in: pilot results
events.purpose: Review pilot stability and wave plans
events.decision: Which pilot findings change how waves 3 and 4 are prepared?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and stability report
Discuss the pilot findings that bear on waves 3 and 4
Confirm the changes to apply to the coming waves

events.label: Workshop 2: waves 3 and 4
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting rollout waves 3 and 4 as planned?
agenda: Present the go-live record for waves 1 and 2
Review pilot and wave results against the plan for waves 3 and 4
Decide whether waves 3 and 4 start as planned

events.label: Final readout
events.decision: Approve the system as running in all 40 pharmacies and close the engagement?
agenda: Present the final readout and go-live record for all 40 pharmacies
Review results against the goal of running in all 40 pharmacies
Decide on approval and closing the engagement

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so every duration is an estimate, about 33 to 39 weeks in total, to confirm before quoting.
Implementation is estimated at 21 to 31 weeks and planned at the middle, 25 to 27; more process areas or slower waves push it higher.
Process areas are assumed at 4; each extra pair adds 5 to 8 weeks across Diagnostic and Implementation, so confirm the count with the client.
No formal tender is planned in Design; if the client must run one or the contract is large, Design grows by 4 to 6 weeks.
Configuration and data migration rehearsal share one stream, and rollout waves run as two paired streams, to keep four streams in Implementation.
No finance owner is listed, yet the vendor selection gate rests on a business case; confirm who signs off the figures.

sub_questions.question: What do the pharmacies' process areas require from a new point-of-sale system?
Which point-of-sale system best meets those requirements and holds up in a business case?
Can the chosen system be configured, loaded with the pharmacies' data and run stably at a pilot pharmacy?
How is the system rolled out in waves until it runs in all 40 pharmacies?

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Process area mapped with its requirements

phases.why: Process areas mapped two at a time, in two rounds, between a start-up week and a synthesis week. Within typical 3 to 6 weeks.

phases.name: Design
phases.why: Vendor shortlist, demonstrations and scoring run once, with one week at the end to synthesize for the gate; no formal tender assumed.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: System configured and tested for one process area
Rollout wave of up to 10 sites

phases.why: Four process areas configured two at a time, then migration rehearsal, pilot site, and four rollout waves of up to 10 sites, one after another.

sizing.levers: Running two rollout waves at once would shorten the engagement most; configuring fewer process areas before the pilot site is the next lever.
